title: How do you check if your ETFs overlap?
summary: Compare what each fund holds by weight, not by count, then look through all your funds at once to see how much of each company you really own.
body_markdown:
## How does Astor help with ETF overlap?


Astor does the whole-portfolio check for you, for free. Connect your brokerage, retirement and crypto accounts, like Robinhood, Schwab and Coinbase, and Astor sees every fund and stock you hold in one place. Ask whether your ETFs overlap and it compares their holdings. Ask how much of a company you really own and it looks through every ETF in every connected account, adds any shares you hold directly and breaks the total down by fund. It’s free to start with no card, and the free plan includes a limited number of questions.


Then it tells you what to do about it. Astor is an SEC-registered investment adviser, so its answers are personalized advice about what you own. If two funds track the same index, it can tell you that one of them adds nothing and which one to keep. If a few companies have crept up through several funds, it explains how concentrated you are, whether that fits what you’re trying to do and how you could bring it down, like trimming a sector fund or choosing a broader one for new money. If the overlap is a tilt you chose on purpose, it tells you that too. You make every decision.


Astor also follows every position you own and texts you on iPhone, iMessage or WhatsApp when something affecting one of them crosses a line you care about. It can see your holdings but can’t move money.
